Finite-element assembly

Source: R/assembly.R
assemble_matrix.Rd

assemble_matrix() assembles a global sparse matrix from element contributions using sparse triplets, which are summed into a compressed column dgCMatrix. Element integrals use triangle quadrature exact to quad_degree (default 2 p + 2 for degree p), which is exact for constant and affine coefficients.

Usage

assemble_matrix(
  space,
  type = c("stiffness", "mass", "advection"),
  coef = NULL,
  t = NULL,
  quad_degree = NULL
)

assemble_vector(space, f, t = NULL, quad_degree = NULL)

assemble_boundary_matrix(
  space,
  alpha = 1,
  marker = "boundary",
  t = NULL,
  quad_degree = NULL
)

assemble_boundary_vector(
  space,
  g,
  marker = "boundary",
  t = NULL,
  quad_degree = NULL
)

Arguments

space

An fe_space().

type

Matrix type.

coef

Coefficient, see Details.

t

Optional time passed to time-dependent coefficients.

quad_degree

Quadrature exactness degree.

f, g, alpha

Scalar coefficients (numbers or function(x, y), or function(x, y, t) together with t).

marker

Boundary markers.

Value

A sparse dgCMatrix or a numeric vector.

Details

Matrix types (i is the test function, j the trial function):

  • "stiffness": K_ij = int k grad(phi_j) . grad(phi_i); coef is the diffusion k (number, function or 2 by 2 matrix for a constant tensor).

  • "mass": M_ij = int c phi_j phi_i; coef defaults to 1.

  • "advection": C_ij = int (b . grad(phi_j)) phi_i; coef is the velocity b (length-2 vector or function(x, y) returning a two column matrix).

assemble_vector() assembles F_i = int f phi_i. assemble_boundary_matrix() and assemble_boundary_vector() assemble int_Gamma alpha phi_j phi_i ds and int_Gamma g phi_i ds over boundary edges with the given markers, using Gauss-Legendre rules on each edge.

Examples

V <- fe_space(pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 4))
K <- assemble_matrix(V, "stiffness")
M <- assemble_matrix(V, "mass")
sum(M)                                  # area of the domain
#> [1] 1
max(abs(K %*% rep(1, V$ndof)))          # constants are in the kernel
#> [1] 0
